rationale: Extends the configuration-recovery account with receipt 4178d9d5c479470cafb7ebd7951a9332 (a voter that recovers no configuration never attempts candidacy) and strengthens the observation-window counter with that receipt's control samples.

interpretations.rationale: Extension note: this successor adds receipt 4178d9d5c479470cafb7ebd7951a9332, which observes in a three-voter group that a node recovering without a configuration never attempts candidacy while the same node and log with the replay disabled do; the sources, the three earlier executions, the knowledge uses, the conclusion and the remaining counterevidence are otherwise unchanged, and the counter about the observation window is strengthened with the new control's sample counts. Correction note: this successor differs from the previous account of this question only by a transcribed latency; the control's election is now stated as the receipt records it (19 polls at a 5ms interval, about 95ms), not from an earlier construction run. Everything else - sources, executions, knowledge uses, counterevidence and limitations - is unchanged. Recovery. Receipt 9a373c13725a42aa9f48f59c0f2f2f1c restarted four real single-voter prefixes on their retained stores with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs on and off: with the flag on and no snapshot the node recovered an empty configuration (event 2: no members at index 0, 268 polls without a leader) although its log holds the bootstrap configuration entry at index 1 (event 0), the flag-off control on the same prefix shape tracked that entry and elected itself (event 6), and with a snapshot taken before a committed AddNonvoter the flag-on node kept the snapshot's index-1 configuration instead of the log's committed index-7 configuration (events 10, 11) while the flag-off control recovered index 7 (event 15). Source side the mechanism is settled: restoreFromCommittedLogs stores the persisted commit index and calls processLogs with it (api.go:723-754), advancing lastApplied before NewRaft runs the scan that rebuilds tracked configuration state from max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 (api.go:602-621), so committed configuration entries at or below that bound never reach processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go:1605-1624) and the FSM's ConfigurationStore is never read back. That state decides election eligibility (raft.go:225-246), quorum size (raft.go:1085-1094), the leader's commitment membership (raft.go:456-467, commitment.go:35-64) and vote admission. First consequence: receipt 79a9cc34b3ce42e197c384775efecc3a removed server C from {A,B,C} (event 2: committed configuration at index 5 with two voters), restarted A with the flag on while B was partitioned, and A tracked the snapshot's index-1 three-voter configuration containing C (event 3); A won the election counting C and committed 'stale-quorum-entry' at index 10 term 4 with apply_error null, its FSM applied it, B's log lacked that index and C's log held it at the same term (event 4). Since A's own match cannot form a majority of three and B had no transport path, the deciding acknowledgement can only have come from C: the entry was committed, applied and reported successful against a member set that is not a majority of the committed configuration. Authority attempt. Receipt 4178d9d5c479470cafb7ebd7951a9332 builds a three-voter group, commits three commands so the staged commit index is non-zero, restarts A over its own stores and reads its tracked configuration: with the replay enabled A tracks no configuration at all (event 15: latest_config_index 0, no members, staged commit index 4), and in 266 samples over 1500ms of hearing no leader with the other voters shut down it was a follower in every sample and never a candidate (event 16, comparison violated); with the replay disabled the same node and the same log recover the three-voter configuration (event 17: latest_config_index 1, three members) and the node was a candidate in 254 of 266 samples, ending in state Candidate (event 18, comparison holds). A node whose tracked configuration is empty therefore does not merely fail to win an election: it never attempts to acquire authority, so it cannot be the source of a new leader even when the surviving members could form a quorum with it. Second consequence, durable: receipt c477da09810f4842ba55130320e2a6b5 leaves A in that recovered state on a three-voter cluster (event 6: latest_config_index 0 with no members and committed_config_index 0, against its log's index-1 three-voter entry and staged commit index 4), takes a snapshot through the library's normal path, and reads back metadata recording no configuration at index 0 while the log establishes a three-voter configuration at index 1 (event 7, snapshot_config_matches_log_config false). A then restarts on the same stores with the replay disabled and comes up with an empty configuration at index 0, no leader within 1500ms, in state Follower (event 8). The loss is therefore not confined to the replay path: once written, the snapshot metadata re-imposes it on a restart that never enables the feature. Defect account: with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a commit-tracking log store, NewRaft cannot roll the node's tracked membership configuration forward past max(snapshot index, persisted commit index), so the node may keep an older or empty membership although its own log already contains the committed configuration entries; the recovered node can be permanently unable to participate, can decide leadership and commit index from a member set the committed configuration does not match - committing an entry a real voter of that configuration does not hold - and can write the lost configuration into durable snapshot metadata, from which later restarts, including ones with the feature disabled, restore it. The library's own test for the feature (raft_test.go:1183-1270) restarts with a snapshot whose configuration already equals the final configuration and asserts only the applied index, so it does not constrain this path. The failed first execution of the multi-node experiment (receipt 4ed46b198c8d41618cc855df0a63d469, exit 1) is retained in the run's logs but is not cited as an execution here: it stopped in the harness at the snapshot step because the elected leader was not the node being snapshotted, so it produced no comparison result about the target.

knowledge.assertion: The startup configuration scan runs from max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1, so entries at or below that bound never reach processConfigurationLogEntry at startup.
restoreFromCommittedLogs stores the store's commit index and calls processLogs with it only when the flag is set, which advances lastApplied to that index before the scan runs.
processConfigurationLogEntry is the only writer of the tracked configuration state; FSM-side configuration storage does not feed back into it.
The tracked latest configuration feeds quorumSize, the leader's commitment membership, leader-lease voter counting and the vote-admission checks.
A follower with configurations.latestIndex equal to 0 does not start an election, which is terminal when no reachable peer can supply a configuration entry.
Snapshots record the committed configuration and its index that the node currently tracks, and startup restores that metadata into the tracked configuration.

counterevidence: The doc comment for RestoreCommittedLogs (config.go:243-254) promises only that committed logs are replayed to catch the FSM up and says nothing about membership recovery, so the stale tracked configuration can be read as an unnamed side effect of a feature that never claimed to preserve it. The counter is that the startup scan at api.go:610-621 exists to rebuild that state from the log, and the observed consequences are a commit decided against a member set the committed configuration does not contain and a durable record that re-imposes the loss.

The commit-rule violation needs the removed server C to stay reachable after its removal, since its acknowledgement is what the stale majority counted; if it were stopped or unreachable the same stale configuration would instead leave the node unable to commit. The receipt therefore shows one reachable-removed-server case rather than every case.

One could argue the snapshot in the durable-state case is only as good as the state the node tracks, and that a caller should not snapshot a node whose configuration is empty. The counter is that the node is an ordinary cluster member whose own log contains the configuration entries, nothing in the API or the documentation marks its snapshots as unusable, and the resulting metadata then defeats a restart that has the feature disabled, so the corruption outlives the condition that created it.

The flag-off restart's failure to lead could be attributed to the 1500ms observation window rather than to the empty configuration. The counter is the source guard that refuses elections while configurations.latestIndex is zero (raft.go:225-241) plus two controls inside the same window: the single-voter control elected itself in 19 polls of the harness's 5ms interval (receipt 9a373c13725a42aa9f48f59c0f2f2f1c, event 6), and in the authority case the node that recovered its configuration was a candidate in 254 of 266 samples while the node with the empty configuration showed zero candidate samples (receipt 4178d9d5c479470cafb7ebd7951a9332, events 16 and 18).

The harness assigns roles deliberately (A restarts, B is partitioned, leadership is moved with the library's transfer) and it takes the snapshot explicitly rather than through the automatic cadence. Those choices select the scenario but do not supply the stale or empty configuration, which event 6 shows against the node's own log, nor the acknowledgement, which C's log carries.

The first execution of the multi-node experiment failed in the harness before any comparison (receipt 4ed46b198c8d41618cc855df0a63d469) and is retained as a harness artifact; the later receipts contain the same scenario with both defects exercised.

The authority case removes the other voters by shutting them down, so it shows that the defective node never attempts candidacy; it does not show an outage that a correct recovery would have prevented, because the recovered three-voter configuration also lacks a quorum with one voter left. What the receipt adds is the capability difference, not a counterfactual outage.
limitations: All nodes are in-memory transports and stores in one process and the harness uses a test log store whose staging is not atomic with its log writes; the caller-side durability contract of CommitTrackingLogStore is assumed, not verified, and no production store or snapshot store is exercised.

The durable-state case snapshots a node that has no snapshot on its stores and then restarts with the replay disabled; shipping such a snapshot to a follower, or corruption arising from the automatic snapshot cadence, is not exercised, and deleting the corrupt snapshot is not tested as a recovery.

The multi-node case is one prefix shape with one committed removal, keeps the removed server running, and injects no message loss, reordering or crash, so the decision defect is observed under a clean transport.

Schedule variation is limited: the multi-node scenario appears in two receipts with the same operands, the durable-state scenario in one, and the observation windows are 1500ms for non-participation and 2000ms apply timeouts.
interpretations.joint_history: All four receipts are executions of this investigation's fixed experiments on the same captured source revision, in separate workspaces with no shared mutable state. Receipt 9a373c13725a42aa9f48f59c0f2f2f1c established the recovery behaviour on four single-voter prefixes; receipt 79a9cc34b3ce42e197c384775efecc3a exercised the same recovery as the setup of a three-voter cluster and observed the commit-rule consequence; receipt c477da09810f4842ba55130320e2a6b5 contains both that three-voter scenario again (events 0-4, with the same operands: a restart tracking the snapshot's index-1 three-voter configuration against a log whose newest configuration entry is index 4 with two voters, and a commit at index 9 completed with only the removed server's acknowledgement) and the new durable-state scenario (events 5-8, where the same recovery leaves an empty tracked configuration). The repeated scenario reproduces the earlier witness with fresh addresses, so the premises each receipt relies on are observed more than once and the newer receipts only add consequences. Receipt 4178d9d5c479470cafb7ebd7951a9332 uses the same three-voter construction as receipt 79a9cc34b3ce42e197c384775efecc3a and reports the same tracked-configuration operands (latest index, voter count, member ids) after a replay-enabled restart, with the replay-disabled restart of the same node and log as its control.
